name: generate_captions
description: Caption a project from its timeline's audio, writing project["captions"]. Mixes every unmuted video item on every enabled visual track together with every unmuted audio track (voiceover, music, sfx), each at its own timeline position, transcribes that mix (multilingual, timeline-time word timings), groups words into styled caption segments (each with a cap-<n> id), carries every field of the prior caption track but its style and segments (the theme), and keeps its translated rows (lang + translationOf), each found again in the new transcript by its words. Mute is read at generation time only. CLI-subprocess equivalent of the /projects/{id}/captions SSE route. Run async (montaj_step async:true) — transcription takes a while — and poll montaj_step_status. Takes a project id, not a file input.

input.description: No file input — operates on a project by id (see project-id param).

output.description: The caption track JSON ({"style", "segments":[...]}) that was written to project["captions"].

params.name: model
params.description: Whisper model. The default, large-v3-turbo-q5_0, is multilingual and suits every language.

params.name: language
params.description: Language code (e.g. en, es, fr), or 'auto' for language auto-detection.

params.name: style
params.description: Caption animation style. Defaults to the prior caption track's style, then the profile's caption style (a new track also takes the profile's caption font), then 'pop'.

params.name: replace-edited
params.description: Lines a person made or edited are kept and the new captions go around them (the answer names them as keptYours). True replaces them too: only when the person asks.

params.name: script
params.description: The script the speaker read. Defaults to the project's editing prompt (its <tags> left out), so a script given there needs no param; an empty string turns it off. Caption words take its spelling and names on the transcript's timings (a misheard name or word is replaced when the two read alike, a word said twice where the script has it once is one word); words said that are not in it stay as heard. The answer counts `corrected`.
